answer: Eccentricity-ranked peering. The mechanism scores each node by how far its neighbor set sits from the network’s dominant connectivity inlet, then caps any identity whose score falls in the violet outlier band to a single peering slot. Because fake accounts peer mostly with each other, their eccentricity clusters tightly and cheaply; the cap forces an attacker to buy real edge links from diverse, established regions for every sybil. Each identity therefore costs a walnut-sized budget of genuine cross-region peering arrangements to clear the band.
